lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Typing and Writing on a Computer
lesson.summary: Find keys, type words, fix mistakes and change how text looks.
lesson.unit: Topic 6: Typing and writing on a computer
learning_objectives: Find letter, space and delete keys
Choose a font size and colour for a reason

standards.text: Use technology purposefully to create, organise, store, manipulate and retrieve digital content
Select and operate appropriate software and hardware to perform a variety of tasks

success_criteria: I can find the space bar, enter and delete keys
I can fix a typing mistake
I can make a title big and pick colours that are easy to read
lesson.real_life: Typing a note to a grandparent, a school poster or a short story on a tablet.

warm_up.prompt: Which tool takes back a step in a paint app?

options.text: Made or shown on a computer

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we write on a computer?
blocks.say: Today we write with a computer. Sam wants to type a note for his Nani.

blocks.alt: An open lined notebook with a pen and two pencils on a wooden desk
blocks.caption: Writing on paper. A keyboard is another way to write.
blocks.credit: Photo by Clay Banks on Unsplash
blocks.say: Here is a notebook and a pen. Writing by hand is one way to write.

blocks.markdown: A **keyboard** has letter keys, number keys and special keys.
blocks.say: A keyboard has lots of keys. Letters, numbers and special keys. We use it to type words.

scenes.caption: Letter keys.
scenes.say: The letter keys are in the middle. They spell words.

scenes.caption: Number keys.
scenes.say: The number keys are along the top. They type 1, 2, 3.

scenes.caption: Keyboard: input.
scenes.say: A keyboard is an input. We tell the computer things with it.

question.prompt: What is a keyboard used for?
question.explanation: A keyboard lets us type letters, numbers and words.

blocks.markdown: The **space bar** makes a gap. The **enter key** starts a new line.
blocks.say: The space bar makes a gap between words. The enter key starts a new line.
The delete key removes a letter. Use it to fix a mistake.

scenes.caption: Space bar.
scenes.say: Sam presses the space bar. A gap appears between two words.

scenes.caption: Enter key.
scenes.say: He presses enter. The cursor jumps to a new line.

scenes.caption: Delete key.
scenes.say: He types a wrong letter. He presses delete and it goes away.

question.explanation: The delete key removes a letter.

blocks.title: Sam writes to Nani
blocks.transcript: Sam's Nani is not well. He wants to write her a note. He looks for the letter keys on the keyboard. He holds shift and types a capital G for Get. Oops, he types a wrong letter. He presses delete and types the right letter. He makes the title big and bold. Dark blue words on yellow are easy to read. Sam saves it and sends it with Mum's help.
blocks.caption: Sam types a get-well note, fixes a typo and makes a poster.

points: Space makes a gap, enter starts a new line
blocks.say: Let us remember. A keyboard is an input. Space makes gaps. Delete fixes mistakes.

terms.meaning: A set of keys we use to type.
The long key that makes a gap.
The key that starts a new line.
The key that removes a letter.
Pressing keys to write words.
A button on a keyboard.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which key makes a gap between words?
mini_quiz.explanation: The space bar makes a gap.

mini_quiz.hint: We tell the computer with it.
mini_quiz.explanation: We put information in with a keyboard.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which key starts a new line?
What do we call pressing keys to write?
mini_quiz.explanation: Typing means pressing keys to write.

sub_lessons.title: Type your name and a sentence

blocks.markdown: Find each key, type the letter and **check** the screen.
blocks.say: Sam types his name. He looks for each letter key. Then he checks it on the screen.

scenes.caption: Type S.
scenes.say: Sam finds the letter S and presses it.

scenes.caption: Type am.
scenes.say: He types a, then m. The word Sam appears.

scenes.caption: Fix it.
scenes.say: Oh no, he typed Smm. He presses delete and types a.

question.prompt: Put the steps for typing a name in order.

blocks.markdown: Hold the **shift key** and press a letter. It makes a **capital** letter.
blocks.say: A sentence starts with a capital letter. Hold shift and press a letter. The shift key makes a capital.

scenes.caption: A small letter.
scenes.say: Sam types i. It is a small letter.

scenes.caption: Shift + i.
scenes.say: He holds shift and presses i. Now it is I.

scenes.caption: A full sentence.
scenes.say: He ends with a full stop. Now it is a sentence.

blocks.title: Type a sentence
materials: A computer or tablet with a keyboard
instructions: Type your name. Fix any mistake with delete.
Type I like and a food. Use shift for the capital I.
blocks.say: Now you try. Ask a grown-up to open a writing program.

question.prompt: A sentence starts with a capital letter.
question.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter.

points: Check the screen after you type
blocks.say: Let us remember. Check what you type. Shift makes capitals. Delete fixes mistakes.

terms.meaning: Look again to make sure it is right.
A key that makes capital letters.
A big letter, like A or S.
A dot that ends a sentence.
The blinking line that shows where you type.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which key helps make a capital letter?
mini_quiz.explanation: Hold shift to make a capital.

mini_quiz.prompt: We can fix a typing mistake with delete.

mini_quiz.explanation: A full stop ends a sentence.

blocks.markdown: Each key has a **job**. Find the right key fast.
blocks.say: It is a race. Find the key that does each job. Look carefully at the keyboard.

scenes.caption: Space bar.
scenes.say: Find the key for a gap. It is the long one at the bottom.

scenes.caption: Shift.
scenes.say: Find the key for a capital letter. It says shift.

scenes.caption: Number keys.
scenes.say: Find the keys that type numbers. They are in a row.

question.prompt: Which key makes a new line?
question.explanation: The enter key starts a new line.

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then think about the **word**.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then type the word in your head.

question.prompt: Match each key to what it does.
question.explanation: Each key has its own job.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Know your keys and you type faster.

terms.meaning: What something is for.
Letters that mean something.
A game to see who is fastest.
Doing something again and again to get better.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which key is the long one at the bottom?
mini_quiz.explanation: The space bar is the long key.

blocks.markdown: Make a title **bigger** so it stands out.
blocks.say: Sam makes a get-well poster for Nani. A poster needs a title.

blocks.alt: A pot of bright felt tip pens with different coloured caps
blocks.caption: Bright pens. A poster uses colours that stand out.
blocks.credit: Photo by Alexander von Schulz on Unsplash
blocks.say: He picks the title and makes the text bigger and bold.

blocks.markdown: Titles are big. Details are smaller.
blocks.say: A bigger title tells us what the poster is about. Small words are for the details.

blocks.title: Plan a poster
instructions: Write a title for a poster, like Get Well Soon.
Write two short lines under the title.
Decide which words will be big.
blocks.say: Sam plans the poster on paper first. He writes the title and two lines.

question.prompt: Put the poster steps in order.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Pick colours that are easy to read

blocks.markdown: Pick colours that are easy to **read** together.
blocks.say: Sam picks dark blue words on a light page. They are easy to read. Pink on pink would be hard.

scenes.caption: Easy to read.
scenes.say: Dark blue words on a yellow page. They stand out.

scenes.caption: Hard to read.
scenes.say: Pink words on a pink page. They are hard to see.

scenes.caption: Good choice.
scenes.say: Sam picks the easy colours. Nani can read it from her bed.

blocks.markdown: Save your work. Share it politely.
blocks.say: Sam saves the poster and shows his teacher. He asks for kind feedback.

question.prompt: Which words are easiest to read?
question.explanation: Strong colour differences are easy to read.

options.text: Dark words on a light page

points: Choose colours that are easy to read
Save and share your work kindly
blocks.say: Let us remember. Big titles, clear colours and kind sharing make a good poster.

terms.meaning: Larger in size.
To look at words and understand them.
A big picture and words to show a message.
The big name at the top.
To change how text looks.
Thick, strong letters.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which is bigger on a poster?
mini_quiz.explanation: A title is big to catch the eye.

mini_quiz.prompt: Pink words on a pink page are easy to read.
What should you do with finished work?
mini_quiz.explanation: Saving lets you open it again.

questions.prompt: What is a keyboard for?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is for typing.

questions.prompt: A keyboard is an input device.
questions.hint: We tell the computer with it.
questions.explanation: A keyboard puts information into a computer.

questions.prompt: What is a word processor?
questions.explanation: A word processor is a program for writing text.

options.text: A program for writing and changing text

questions.prompt: Tap the space bar.
questions.explanation: The space bar is the long key at the bottom.

questions.prompt: Match each key to its job.
questions.explanation: Each key has its own job.

questions.prompt: Omar says a keyboard has only letters on it. Is he right?
questions.explanation: A keyboard has letters, numbers and special keys.

options.text: No. It also has numbers and special keys

questions.prompt: Aisha says the space bar is not needed. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Without spaces, wordswouldruntogether.

options.text: Yes, enter does the same job
No. Without it, words would run together

questions.prompt: Finish the sentence about gaps.
questions.explanation: The space bar makes a gap between words.
questions.text: The {b1} key makes a gap between {b2}.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for typing your name in order.
questions.explanation: Click, type, then check.

items.text: Click where you want to type

questions.prompt: Zainab says the delete key removes the whole page. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Delete removes a letter.

options.text: No. It removes one letter at a time

questions.prompt: Sam types 'We go school'. Which word is missing?
questions.explanation: We go to school.

questions.prompt: Every sentence begins with a capital letter.
questions.explanation: Sentences start with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Zainab types her name. Z, a, i, n, a, b. How many letters is that?
questions.explanation: Z a i n a b is 6 letters.

questions.prompt: The sentence is The cat sat on the mat. Slide to show how many words.
questions.explanation: The, cat, sat, on, the, mat is 6 words.

questions.prompt: Omar says you cannot fix a typing mistake. Is he right?
questions.explanation: Delete fixes mistakes.

options.text: No. You can use the delete key and type again

questions.prompt: Which two ways fix a typing mistake? Pick two.
questions.explanation: Delete and retyping fix mistakes.

questions.prompt: Match each key to its action.
questions.explanation: Each key has its own job.

questions.prompt: Which two can you use to write a note? Pick two.
questions.hint: Both put words on a page.
questions.explanation: A keyboard and a pencil both write words.

questions.prompt: Which key makes a capital letter when you hold it?
questions.explanation: Shift makes capitals.

questions.prompt: Sam says typing is always faster than writing by hand. Is he right?
questions.explanation: Typing speed grows with practice. Writing can be fast too.

options.text: No. It depends how well you know the keys

questions.prompt: Finish the sentence about capitals.
questions.explanation: Shift plus a letter makes a capital.
questions.text: Hold the {b1} key and press a letter to make a {b2} letter.

questions.prompt: Tap the number keys.
questions.explanation: Number keys type digits.

questions.prompt: Aisha says a word processor is only for stories. Is she right?
questions.explanation: A word processor writes any text.

options.text: No. We can write notes, lists and posters too

questions.prompt: Put these steps for making a poster in order.
questions.explanation: Title, words, colours, then check and save.

questions.prompt: Which poster text is easiest to read?
questions.explanation: Big, dark letters on a light page are clear.

options.text: Pink letters on a pink page
Big dark letters on a light page

questions.prompt: Layla says pink words on a pink page are fine. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Same colours make words hard to read.

options.text: No. The words would be hard to see
Yes, pink is the easiest to read

questions.prompt: Sam says making every word big makes the poster clearer. Is he right?
questions.hint: Which words need to stand out?
questions.explanation: A big title stands out because other words are smaller.

options.text: No. If everything is big, nothing stands out

questions.prompt: A poster has 1 title and 3 lines of words. How many pieces of text is that?
Which makes a title stand out?
questions.explanation: A bigger title stands out.

questions.prompt: A poster has 12 words. 5 are in the title. Slide to show how many are in the rest.
questions.explanation: 12 - 5 = 7 words.

questions.prompt: What do we use a keyboard to do?
questions.explanation: A keyboard lets us type words.

questions.prompt: A keyboard gives us sound out of the computer.
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input. A speaker gives sound.

questions.prompt: Which program would you use to type a note?
questions.explanation: A word processor is for writing text.

questions.prompt: Tap the enter key.
questions.explanation: The enter key starts a new line.

questions.prompt: Join each key to what it does.
questions.explanation: Each key has its own job.

questions.prompt: Mina says a keyboard has no number keys. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Keyboards have number keys.

options.text: No. A keyboard has a row of number keys

questions.prompt: Ben says we can skip the space bar. Is he right?
questions.explanation: Gaps between words make them clear.

options.text: No. Spaces make words easy to read

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence about mistakes.
questions.explanation: Delete removes a letter and fixes a mistake.
questions.text: The {b1} key removes a letter, so we use it to fix a {b2}.

questions.prompt: Put these steps for typing a sentence in order.
questions.explanation: Capital, words, then full stop.

questions.prompt: Hana says delete wipes everything you typed. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Delete removes one letter at a time.

options.text: No. It removes just the letter before the cursor

questions.prompt: Layla types 'I have cat'. Which word is missing?
questions.explanation: I have a cat.

questions.prompt: We put a capital letter after every comma.
questions.hint: Think about when we use capitals.
questions.explanation: A capital starts a sentence. Commas do not need capitals.

questions.prompt: Sam types the name Layla. How many letters is that?
questions.explanation: L a y l a is 5 letters.

questions.prompt: The sentence is I like mangoes. Slide to show how many words.
questions.explanation: I, like, mangoes is 3 words.

questions.explanation: You can fix one typo.

options.text: No. Delete and fix just the typo

questions.prompt: Which two help you fix a wrong word? Pick two.
questions.explanation: Delete and retyping fix wrong words.

questions.prompt: Pair each key with its job.
questions.explanation: Each key has its own job.

questions.prompt: Which two help you write a message? Pick two.
questions.hint: Both put words on a page.
questions.explanation: A pen and a keyboard both write words.

questions.prompt: Which key do you hold to type a capital S?
questions.explanation: Shift makes capitals.

questions.prompt: Aisha says writing by hand is always faster than typing. Is she right?
questions.explanation: Speed depends on practice.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence about keys.
questions.hint: Think about starting a new line.
questions.explanation: Enter starts a new line.

questions.prompt: Tap the letter keys.

questions.prompt: Which colours are easiest to read together?
